lessons.title: Notre voyage en français
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on their French learning journey throughout the year
materials: Photo albums or work samples from each month

opening.activity: Show calendar from September to now. Say 'Regardons notre voyage!' Use hand gesture of traveling/walking to introduce 'voyage'. Point to different months and ask students what they remember.
opening.connection: This begins our journey of looking back at all we've learned this year

mainActivity.activity: Journey Timeline - Create a visual timeline of the school year on the floor using masking tape. Students walk along the timeline, stopping at different months to share memories of French learning. Teacher adds pictures/artifacts at each stop.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may remember more than others - encourage any memory sharing. Let visual learners look at photos to trigger memories.

closing.activity: Journey Reflection - Students sit in circle and each shares one word (in French or English) to describe their French learning journey this year.

decisionPoints.decision: How much French growth can students recognize in themselves?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If they need prompting → Use specific examples and before/after comparisons. If they recognize growth → Encourage them to share specific examples

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need visual supports to remember earlier learning?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Use photos, work samples, and concrete artifacts from each month. If no → Use verbal prompts and discussion

decisionPoints.decision: Should we use photos or work samples to trigger memories?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students are struggling to remember → Use physical artifacts and photos. If memories are flowing → Continue with discussion

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students can't remember early learning, focus on recent memories and work backwards. If they get too nostalgic or sad, emphasize growth and celebration.
lessons.realWorldConnection: People look back on their year to see how much they've grown and learned - like looking through photo albums with family

lessons.title: Nos premiers mots français
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate the first French words they learned

opening.activity: Show timeline from yesterday and point to September. Ask 'Quels étaient nos premiers mots?' Show 'premier' with finger gesture (number 1) and 'célébrer' with clapping.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing specifically on early vocabulary acquisition

mainActivity.activity: First Words Treasure Hunt - Hide early vocabulary cards around the room (bonjour, au revoir, merci, oui, non, etc.). Students find cards and try to remember learning these words. Create a 'First Words Hall of Fame' poster together.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may remember learning context, others just the words. Both are valuable to share.

closing.activity: First Words Celebration - Class says each first word together with original actions/gestures. End with appreciation: 'Nous avons bien appris!'

decisionPoints.decision: Which early French words do students still remember?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If they remember many → Celebrate and add more challenging early words. If few → Focus on most basic greetings and responses

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need prompting with pictures or gestures?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Use original teaching gestures and visual supports. If no → Let them recall independently

decisionPoints.decision: Should we recreate some early learning activities?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students enjoy nostalgia → Repeat simple early activities. If they seem bored → Focus on how much they've grown since then

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students have forgotten too many early words, turn it into a re-learning celebration. If they're frustrated by their 'baby' learning, emphasize how these were building blocks.
lessons.realWorldConnection: We remember our 'firsts' - first words, first steps, first day of school - they're special milestones

lessons.title: Chansons et comptines préférées
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and perform favorite French songs and rhymes from the year
materials: Song lyric charts from the year

opening.activity: Hum a familiar French tune from early in the year. Ask students to identify it. Introduce 'chanson' with singing gesture and 'comptine' with rhythmic clapping.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 2 by celebrating musical and rhythmic language learning

mainActivity.activity: Musical Memory Lane - Vote on favorite songs/rhymes from the year. Perform top 3-4 choices with original actions. Students can suggest new movements or variations. Create a 'Greatest Hits' list.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let confident singers lead, but encourage everyone to participate at their comfort level. Some may prefer actions over singing.

closing.activity: Song Circle - Sit in circle and each student hums or sings one line from their personal favorite French song from the year.

decisionPoints.decision: Which songs do students remember most clearly?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If they remember many → Let them choose favorites to perform. If few → Review and re-teach beloved songs

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need lyric supports or can they sing from memory?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need support → Provide lyric charts or picture cues. If know by heart → Encourage memory singing

decisionPoints.decision: Should we add new movements to familiar songs?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students are creative → Let them choreograph new movements. If prefer familiar → Stick with original actions

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students have forgotten song words, focus on rhythm and melody. If they're too energetic, use quieter songs or seated activities.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Music helps us remember and connects us to happy memories - like family songs or lullabies from childhood

lessons.title: Histoires que nous aimons
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit favorite French stories and books from throughout the year
materials: French books read throughout the year

opening.activity: Show stack of French books from the year. Ask 'Quelle histoire préférez-vous?' Show 'aimer' with heart gesture over chest.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 3 by celebrating narrative and reading experiences

mainActivity.activity: Story Museum - Set up stations with different beloved books from the year. Students rotate through stations, looking at books and sharing memories of each story. Vote on class favorite and reread together.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want to 'read' independently, others prefer group sharing. Both are valuable.

closing.activity: Story Sharing Circle - Each student shows their favorite page from the winning book and says why they like it (can use English if needed).

decisionPoints.decision: Which stories had the biggest impact on students?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If clear favorites emerge → Focus on those for deeper discussion. If many different preferences → Celebrate variety

decisionPoints.decision: Do they remember story details or just general impressions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If details remembered → Encourage retelling and discussion. If general impressions → Focus on feelings and favorites

decisionPoints.decision: Should we reread stories or just look at pictures and discuss?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students want full rereading → Choose one favorite for complete reread. If prefer browsing → Let them explore multiple books

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students disagree about favorites, celebrate different tastes. If attention wanes during rereading, switch to picture walks and discussion.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Favorite stories stay with us and shape how we see the world - like bedtime stories that become lifelong memories

lessons.title: Nos réussites en français
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify and celebrate specific French learning achievements

opening.activity: Show examples of student work from September vs. now. Point out growth and say 'Regardez vos réussites!' Show 'fier' with proud posture and big smile.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 4 by moving from content review to metacognitive reflection

mainActivity.activity: Achievement Gallery Walk - Display student work from throughout the year. Students walk around and place gold stars on work that shows their growth or makes them proud. Discuss what makes each piece special.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students readily identify achievements, others need prompting. Help all students find something to celebrate.

closing.activity: Pride Circle - Each student shares one thing they're proud of learning in French this year. Class responds with 'Bravo!' and applause.

decisionPoints.decision: Can students articulate what they're proud of learning?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Encourage specific examples and reasons. If struggling → Provide examples and help them recognize growth

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need examples to recognize their own growth?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Show before/after work samples and point out improvements. If no → Let them self-identify achievements

decisionPoints.decision: Should achievements be academic or social/emotional?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If focusing on academics → Highlight language growth and skills. If broader view → Include confidence, friendship, effort

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students are too critical of early work, reframe as 'brave first attempts.' If they can't identify achievements, help them see progress in participation or effort.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing our achievements helps build confidence and motivation - like celebrating learning to ride a bike or swim

lessons.title: Défis surmontés ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on challenges they overcame in French learning

opening.activity: Remind students of early year challenges (silent period, new sounds, etc.). Show 'défi' with barrier gesture, then 'surmonter' with climbing over motion.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 5 by acknowledging growth through overcoming difficulties

mainActivity.activity: Challenge Champions - Discuss common challenges from the year (pronunciation, understanding, participating). Students share how they or classmates helped overcome these. Create a 'Challenge Champions' poster showing strategies.
mainActivity.flexibility: Frame all challenges positively as learning opportunities. Some students may need encouragement to share struggles.

closing.activity: Strength Circle - Each student names one way they helped themselves or a classmate overcome a French challenge this year.

decisionPoints.decision: Are students comfortable discussing things that were difficult?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If uncomfortable → Focus on how challenges are normal and lead to growth. If comfortable → Encourage honest sharing

decisionPoints.decision: Should challenges be framed positively as growth opportunities?
decisionPoints.ifThen: Always frame positively → Use 'learning opportunities' and 'growth challenges.' Avoid negative language about struggles

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need support to see how they overcame difficulties?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Provide specific examples and celebrate problem-solving strategies. If no → Let them identify their own growth

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students become discouraged thinking about challenges, immediately pivot to celebrating growth and support. If they minimize their challenges, validate that learning French is genuinely hard work.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone faces challenges, and overcoming them makes us stronger - like learning to ride a bike or make new friends

lessons.title: Amis et moments spéciaux
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on friendships and special moments in French class

opening.activity: Show photos of students working together during the year. Ask 'Qui sont vos amis en français?' Show 'spécial' with hands making heart shape.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 6 by celebrating social and emotional aspects of learning

mainActivity.activity: Memory Sharing Circle - Students take turns sharing a special moment with a friend in French class. Could be helping each other, laughing together, or collaborative successes. Create memory cards to keep.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may be shy about naming friends. Allow general sharing about good times with classmates.

closing.activity: Friendship Appreciation - Students give compliments to classmates about their French learning journey: 'Merci [name] pour...' with teacher translation support.

decisionPoints.decision: How comfortable are students sharing positive peer relationships?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If comfortable → Encourage specific friendship stories. If shy → Focus on general class community and teamwork

decisionPoints.decision: Should focus be on group memories or individual friendships?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If strong friendships exist → Celebrate individual connections. If class dynamic is more general → Focus on whole group experiences

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need prompting to remember collaborative learning moments?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Show photos and provide specific examples. If no → Let them share freely from memory

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If any student feels left out, emphasize everyone's contributions to the class community. If conflicts arise, focus on positive growth and shared experiences.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning is more meaningful when we share it with friends - like playing games or exploring new places together

lessons.title: Créations dont nous sommes fiers
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate creative work produced throughout the year
materials: Student art work and projects from year

opening.activity: Set up a mini art gallery with student work from the year. Say 'Voici nos créations!' Show 'fier' with proud stance and big smile.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 7 by focusing on tangible evidence of learning and creativity

mainActivity.activity: Artist Gallery Walk - Students walk through display of their creative work (art, writing, projects) from the year. Each student chooses their proudest creation to present to the class with simple explanation.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may want to present multiple pieces, others may be shy. Adjust presentation length and format based on student comfort.

closing.activity: Creator's Circle - Each student holds their chosen creation and receives applause from classmates. End with group cheer: 'Nous sommes des artistes!'

decisionPoints.decision: Which student creations show the most growth or effort?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If clear examples → Highlight growth and effort over perfection. If all work looks similar → Focus on personal meaning and pride

decisionPoints.decision: Should we display work or have students present it?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students enjoy presenting → Give each child presentation time. If shy group → Focus on gallery walk and appreciation

decisionPoints.decision: Do they remember the process of creating or just the final products?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If remember process → Discuss learning journey and challenges overcome. If just products → Focus on final achievements

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students are critical of their early work, emphasize growth and learning journey. If some work looks less developed, highlight effort and personal meaning.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists and creators look back at their work to see their journey - like looking through a photo album or memory book

lessons.title: Commencer notre portfolio
lessons.oneGoal: Students begin organizing their year's work into a meaningful portfolio

opening.activity: Show an example portfolio. Explain 'portfolio' as a special book of our best work. Show 'organiser' by sorting papers into groups.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 8 by transitioning from reflection to documentation and organization

mainActivity.activity: Portfolio Organization - Students begin sorting their work into categories (writing, art, photos, certificates). Start organizing chronologically or by theme. Teacher circulates to help with decision-making.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want thematic organization, others chronological. Both approaches are valid.

closing.activity: Organization Share - Students show their portfolio start to a partner and explain their organization system.

decisionPoints.decision: How much independence can students handle in portfolio organization?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If highly independent → Let them create their own systems. If need guidance → Provide templates and categories

decisionPoints.decision: Should portfolios be chronological or thematic?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students show preference → Support their choice. If uncertain → Suggest chronological as simpler option

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need templates or can they create their own structure?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If creative and organized → Encourage personal structure. If overwhelmed → Provide simple templates

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students become overwhelmed with choices, provide simple 2-3 category system. If they want to include everything, help them select most meaningful pieces.
lessons.realWorldConnection: People create portfolios to show their best work and growth over time - like photo albums or memory books

lessons.title: Choisir nos meilleurs exemples
lessons.oneGoal: Students select their best work samples for portfolio inclusion

opening.activity: Continue portfolio work from yesterday. Show 'choisir' with selection gestures. Discuss what makes work 'meilleur' - effort, growth, pride, learning shown.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 9 by developing critical thinking and self-evaluation skills

mainActivity.activity: Best Work Selection - Students review all their work and select pieces that show: 1) Their best effort, 2) Their growth, 3) Their learning, 4) Work they're proud of. Use simple criteria checklist to guide decisions.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want to include everything, others may be too selective. Guide them toward balanced representation.

closing.activity: Selection Reflection - Students place selected work in portfolios and share with partner why each piece was chosen.

decisionPoints.decision: What criteria should students use to select 'best' work?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need clear criteria → Use effort, growth, pride, and learning shown. If intuitive choosers → Let them follow their instincts

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need guidance on variety vs. quality?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If choosing all same type → Encourage variety across subjects/formats. If good variety → Support their choices

decisionPoints.decision: Should selection focus on growth evidence or final products?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If process-focused → Include before/after examples showing growth. If product-focused → Include best final pieces

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students can't decide, help them by asking what they're proudest of. If they choose only perfect work, help them see value in growth examples.
lessons.realWorldConnection: We choose our best examples when applying for jobs or showing our abilities - like when we show our best drawings to family

lessons.title: Raconter notre histoire d'apprentissage
lessons.oneGoal: Students create narratives explaining their learning journey and growth

opening.activity: Look at completed portfolio sections. Explain that now we tell the 'histoire' of our learning. Show 'raconter' with storytelling gestures.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 10 by adding reflective narrative to portfolio selections

mainActivity.activity: Learning Story Creation - Students create their learning story using template: 'Au début...', 'Puis...', 'Maintenant...', 'Dans le futur...' Can be written, drawn, or recorded orally with teacher support.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may prefer drawing their story, others simple writing. Recording oral stories is also valid.

closing.activity: Story Preview - 3-4 students share one sentence from their learning story. Others listen and appreciate.

decisionPoints.decision: Can students articulate their learning story in French?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If yes → Encourage French with teacher support. If no → Allow English with key French phrases

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need sentence starters or story templates?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need structure → Provide clear templates and sentence starters. If creative → Allow free-form storytelling

decisionPoints.decision: Should stories be written, oral, or illustrated?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If writers → Encourage written stories with pictures. If artists → Focus on illustrated stories. If verbal → Record oral stories

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students struggle with narrative format, help them list key moments instead. If they get stuck on details, focus on main feelings and experiences.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has a learning story - how we grew and changed over time - like telling family about school or sharing adventures

lessons.title: Partager avec nos familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students prepare to share their portfolios and growth with families

opening.activity: Show completed portfolios with pride. Explain that we will 'partager' with 'famille'. Show 'montrer' with presentation gestures.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 11 by preparing to communicate learning beyond the classroom

mainActivity.activity: Family Presentation Prep - Students practice showing their portfolios and telling their learning story. Practice key French phrases to share with families: 'Voici mon travail', 'Je suis fier de...', 'J'ai appris...'
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want elaborate presentations, others simple sharing. Both approaches are valid.

closing.activity: Practice Partner Share - Students practice their family presentation with a classmate, giving each other encouragement.

decisionPoints.decision: How comfortable are students presenting their learning to families?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If confident → Encourage detailed presentations. If nervous → Provide simple scripts and support

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need practice or scripts for family presentations?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need scripts → Provide key French phrases and English explanations. If confident → Let them present naturally

decisionPoints.decision: Should sharing be formal presentations or informal conversations?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students prefer formal → Set up presentation format. If prefer casual → Encourage natural sharing conversations

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students are anxious about family sharing, reassure them families will be proud regardless. If they want to share everything, help them choose key highlights.
lessons.realWorldConnection: We share our achievements and growth with people who care about us - like showing report cards or art projects at home

lessons.title: Célébrer nos progrès
lessons.oneGoal: Students participate in a celebration of their French learning progress

opening.activity: Enter classroom decorated for celebration. Announce 'Aujourd'hui nous célébrons!' Show 'grandir' with growing gesture from small to tall.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 12 by formally recognizing and honoring learning achievements

mainActivity.activity: Progress Celebration Festival - Multiple celebration stations: 1) Portfolio viewing, 2) French song performance, 3) Achievement certificate ceremony, 4) Reflection sharing circle. Families invited if possible.
mainActivity.flexibility: Adjust celebration size and format based on class needs and family availability.

closing.activity: Celebration Circle - Everyone (students, families, teacher) stands in circle for final appreciation and group photo.

decisionPoints.decision: What type of celebration would be most meaningful for students?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students love performance → Include singing and presentations. If prefer quiet recognition → Focus on certificates and reflection

decisionPoints.decision: Should celebration be individual recognition or group achievement?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If competitive class → Emphasize individual achievements. If collaborative class → Focus on group accomplishments

decisionPoints.decision: Do families need to be included in the celebration?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If possible → Invite families for portfolio sharing. If not possible → Plan separate family communication

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If celebration becomes overwhelming, simplify to key appreciation moments. If families can't attend, record videos to share later.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrations mark important milestones and achievements in our lives - like birthdays, graduations, or family accomplishments

lessons.title: Regarder vers l'avenir
lessons.oneGoal: Students set goals and express hopes for continued French learning

opening.activity: Look at timeline from Lesson 1, but extend it into the future. Show 'avenir' by pointing ahead, 'espoir' with hopeful gesture, 'continuer' with ongoing motion.
opening.connection: Builds on Lesson 13 by connecting current achievement to future learning possibilities

mainActivity.activity: Future French Dreams - Students create simple goals for continued French learning: 'L'année prochaine, je veux...' Support with pictures and simple phrases. Share hopes for Grade 2 French adventures.
mainActivity.flexibility: Goals can be specific skills or general enthusiasm. Both are valuable for motivation.

closing.activity: Future Circle - Each student shares one hope for their French learning future. Teacher responds with encouragement and belief in their continued growth.

decisionPoints.decision: Are students excited about continuing French or feeling anxious?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If excited → Channel enthusiasm into specific goals. If anxious → Provide reassurance and emphasize past success

decisionPoints.decision: Should goals be specific skills or general enthusiasm?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If concrete thinkers → Help with specific skill goals. If dreamers → Encourage general enthusiasm and love for French

decisionPoints.decision: Do they understand French will continue in their education?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If unclear → Explain French immersion continues through school. If understand → Build excitement for next level

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students are worried about future challenges, remind them of growth they've already shown. If goals are unrealistic, help them set achievable aspirations.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Setting goals helps us continue growing and reaching for new achievements - like planning summer activities or dreaming about what we want to be when we grow up

lessons.title: Jeux de révision amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students play engaging games reviewing vocabulary and concepts from the year

opening.activity: Celebrate completing all core lessons! Show game materials and say 'Maintenant nous jouons!' Show 'amusant' with big smile and playful gesture.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 14 by reinforcing learning through enjoyable review activities

mainActivity.activity: Game Station Carnival - Set up 4 stations: 1) Memory matching with year's vocabulary, 2) Charades with French actions, 3) Musical French freeze dance, 4) Simple French bingo. Rotate every 6-7 minutes.
mainActivity.flexibility: Adjust game difficulty and pace based on student energy and engagement levels.

closing.activity: Game Champions Circle - Everyone gets appreciation for game participation. Vote on favorite game to play again tomorrow.

decisionPoints.decision: Which review games engage students most effectively?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If high energy → Use movement games and competitions. If prefer calm → Use card games and puzzles

decisionPoints.decision: Should games focus on vocabulary, grammar, or communication?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need vocabulary practice → Focus on word games. If communication → Use role-play and conversation games

decisionPoints.decision: Do students prefer competitive or collaborative game formats?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If collaborative class → Use team games and cooperation. If competitive → Use individual challenges with good sportsmanship

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If games become too competitive or chaotic, switch to calmer activities. If students lose interest, let them suggest variations or new games.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing games with what we've learned makes knowledge stick and brings joy - like family game nights or playground games

lessons.title: Spectacle de talents français
lessons.oneGoal: Students showcase their French abilities through performances or presentations

opening.activity: Set up performance area like a talent show. Explain 'spectacle' with stage gestures and 'talent' by pointing to students with pride.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 15 by providing authentic opportunities to demonstrate French proficiency

mainActivity.activity: French Talent Showcase - Students choose how to showcase their French: singing, reciting, storytelling, demonstrating vocabulary, or simple conversations. Everyone performs something, however small.
mainActivity.flexibility: Performance length and complexity should match student comfort levels. Some may do simple vocabulary, others elaborate performances.

closing.activity: Standing Ovation - After all performances, everyone stands for appreciation of courage and French growth shown by all participants.

decisionPoints.decision: What performance formats appeal to different student personalities?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If shy students → Offer group performances or simple demonstrations. If performers → Encourage individual showcases

decisionPoints.decision: Should performances be individual or group-based?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If confident class → Mix individual and group options. If nervous class → Focus on group or partner performances

decisionPoints.decision: Do students need time to prepare or prefer spontaneous sharing?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need preparation → Give planning time and practice. If spontaneous → Encourage natural, unrehearsed sharing

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If stage fright occurs, allow students to perform from their seats or with a partner. If performances run long, set gentle time limits.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Talent shows let us share our abilities and celebrate what makes each person special - like school concerts or family performances

lessons.title: Lettres à nous-mêmes
lessons.oneGoal: Students write letters to their future selves about their French learning experience

opening.activity: Show example of a letter. Explain writing to 'futur' self - the student they will be in Grade 2. Show timeline extending into next year.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 16 by encouraging deeper reflection and connection to future learning

mainActivity.activity: Future Self Letters - Students write simple letters to their Grade 2 selves about French learning: what they learned, what they're proud of, advice for continuing. Use mix of French phrases and English as needed.
mainActivity.flexibility: Letter length and language complexity should match individual abilities. Pictures and simple phrases are perfectly valid.

closing.activity: Letter Sealing Ceremony - Students seal letters in special envelopes to be opened at start of Grade 2 (with teacher coordination).

decisionPoints.decision: Can students write simple letters in French or need English support?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If French capable → Encourage French with English support. If need English → Focus on key French phrases within English letters

decisionPoints.decision: Should letters focus on advice, memories, or encouragement?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If reflective students → Include all elements. If simpler → Focus on encouragement and favorite memories

decisionPoints.decision: Do they understand the concept of 'future self'?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If unclear → Explain as 'you next year' with concrete examples. If understand → Encourage deeper future thinking

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If letter writing is too abstract, help students focus on simple messages like 'Keep trying!' If they worry about forgetting, reassure them the letter will help them remember.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Writing to our future selves helps us remember important moments and lessons - like time capsules or diary entries

lessons.title: Cadeau pour la prochaine classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students create something helpful for next year's Grade 1 French students

opening.activity: Discuss how scary but exciting starting Grade 1 French was. Show 'cadeau' with giving gesture and explain creating something special for new students.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 17 by channeling reflection into service and mentorship

mainActivity.activity: Gift Creation Workshop - Students create welcome gifts for new Grade 1 French students: advice cards, welcome posters, recorded messages, or simple French phrase books. Focus on encouragement and support.
mainActivity.flexibility: Gifts can be individual or collaborative creations. Match complexity to student abilities and interests.

closing.activity: Gift Presentation - Students show their gifts and explain how they will help new French learners feel welcome and confident.

decisionPoints.decision: What would be most helpful for incoming Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If remember early fears → Focus on encouragement and 'you can do it' messages. If remember helpful strategies → Include practical tips

decisionPoints.decision: Should gifts be advice, encouragement, or practical resources?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students prefer emotional support → Focus on encouragement. If practical minded → Include helpful strategies and tips

decisionPoints.decision: Do students remember what would have helped them at the beginning?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If remember clearly → Use their experiences to guide gift creation. If unclear → Help them think about what made them feel safe

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students focus on difficulties rather than encouragement, guide them toward positive, supportive messages. If gifts become too complex, simplify to heartfelt messages.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Helping others who are starting their journey is a way to give back and show growth - like big siblings helping little ones

lessons.title: Temps libre français
lessons.oneGoal: Students engage in free choice French activities based on their interests

opening.activity: Show choice menu of French activities. Explain 'temps libre' - time to choose what they want to do in French. Show 'intérêt' by asking about preferences.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 18 by honoring student voice and choice in their learning

mainActivity.activity: French Choice Time - Students choose from: French books, drawing with French labels, singing French songs, playing French games, or creating with French materials. Teacher supports all choices.
mainActivity.flexibility: Honor all interests and choices. Some may want quiet activities, others collaborative or creative pursuits.

closing.activity: Choice Reflection - Students share what they chose and why. Appreciate the variety of interests and ways to enjoy French.

decisionPoints.decision: What French activities do students choose when given freedom?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If choose familiar activities → Honor comfort with familiar. If choose new challenges → Support exploration

decisionPoints.decision: Should choices be from provided options or completely open?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If need structure → Provide clear menu of options. If independent → Allow open exploration of all French materials

decisionPoints.decision: Do students need guidance to make meaningful choices?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If overwhelmed by choices → Provide categories or suggestions. If decisive → Trust their instincts and interests

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students can't decide, help them remember favorite activities from the year. If choices become chaotic, provide gentle structure while honoring preferences.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Having choices about what we do helps us feel ownership and enjoyment - like choosing what games to play or books to read

lessons.title: Au revoir et à bientôt!
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate the end of Grade 1 French and look forward to continuing

opening.activity: Gather in celebration circle. Explain this is 'au revoir' to Grade 1 French but 'à bientôt' because French learning continues. Show excitement for future.
opening.connection: Extends Lesson 19 by providing closure while maintaining excitement for continued French learning

mainActivity.activity: Final Celebration Festival - Multiple stations: memory book signing, photo taking, favorite activity reprises, future preview, and appreciation circle. End with group performance of favorite French song.
mainActivity.flexibility: Balance celebration with any sadness about ending. Focus on growth achieved and excitement for continued learning.

closing.activity: Final Circle - Everyone shares one word describing their Grade 1 French experience. End with group hug and 'À bientôt!' rather than goodbye.

decisionPoints.decision: How can we make the ending feel celebratory rather than sad?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students are sad → Emphasize this is just the end of Grade 1, French continues. If celebratory → Channel excitement into appreciation

decisionPoints.decision: Should focus be on endings or new beginnings?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If students handle endings well → Acknowledge completion and growth. If endings are hard → Focus on new adventures ahead

decisionPoints.decision: Do students need reassurance about continuing French learning?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If anxious → Provide specific reassurance about Grade 2 French. If excited → Build anticipation for new learning adventures

lessons.whenThingsGoWrong: If students become too emotional, focus on happy memories and future excitement. If celebration becomes overwhelming, simplify to key appreciation moments.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Saying goodbye to one chapter means we're ready to start the next adventure - like finishing a good book and looking for the next one
